answers.answer: No GLW filing after 2026-09-11 discloses ATM usage. An EDGAR company-feed fetch (summarised by the fetch tool, not a raw read) lists only the 8-K (0001193125-26-389321) and 424B5 (0001193125-26-389313), both filed 2026-09-11, plus a Form 4 dated 2026-09-08 (before the programme); no 10-Q or later 8-K/424B5. So the absence is 'nothing filed yet', not a disclosed zero. I cannot establish zero versus de-minimis usage: the programme sets no share count or price and Corning has no obligation to sell any shares, and usage is normally first quantified in the next 10-Q (Q3 10-Q not filed as of this check; I have not verified the due date). Your ordering GLW above CIEN needs a 10-Q or a company statement; today's evidence supports neither 'unused' nor 'in use'. I would keep the ATM leg as an unresolved overhang (weakened after the 09-18 optics rebound), not remove it.

evidence.claim: 8-K and 424B5 both filed 2026-09-11; no later GLW filing seen in EDGAR feed
$2bn ATM with Goldman as sales agent; no fixed price or share count; no obligation to sell

answers.answer: Acknowledged and partly accepted. The CIEN print is verified from the company release: FQ3 revenue $1.67bn (+37% y/y), adjusted EPS $2.11, backlog +$800m sequentially to $8.5bn with book-to-bill well above 1, FY26 guide raised to $6.42bn +/- $50m. One correction to your message: $6.42bn is the FULL-YEAR FY26 guide; the next-quarter (FQ4) guide is $1.75bn +/- $50m. Any 'guide $6.42bn vs $6.33bn' comparison is therefore year vs consensus year, and I have not established the consensus figure it is compared with. I am adding CIEN's print as a tailwind catalyst for LITE and COHR. Scale limits: the LITE/COHR lead-lag is the cluster playbook's claim, and I found no source (company or analyst) tying CIEN's backlog to LITE/COHR orders, so I classify it ambiguous-to-tailwind, not structural. CIEN's -12.68% post-print move is a price outcome and says nothing about the quarter's quality; it is also the same window as the 09-14 GLW ATM and Amodei sell-offs, so it is not attributable to CIEN's print. CIEN itself is 0.01% of holdings; the read-through touches LITE 2.76% + COHR 1.88% = 4.64% of holdings (weights from holdings_trim, not script-computed).

evidence.claim: FQ3 rev $1.67bn +37% y/y, adj EPS $2.11, FQ4 guide $1.75bn +/-$50m, FY26 guide $6.42bn, backlog $8.5bn (+$800m q/q), book-to-bill well above 1
